problem: Prior VLN methods treat REVERIE like fine-grained instruction following, but REVERIE gives only a high-level command and needs goal-oriented exploration. They lack explicit room/object reasoning and prior knowledge, and have weak stopping decisions.
motivation: Finding a remote referred object from a high-level instruction needs commonsense about which rooms contain which objects, so external knowledge (a knowledge graph and pretrained CLIP) can guide decisions. Explicitly decoupling room and object clues, and learning stopping separately, should improve efficiency and success.
key_idea: Decouple room and object entities in instruction and observation (ROA), reason over them with knowledge graph and CLIP-prompted knowledge (KERR+ with Entity Prompter), and learn stopping with an RL-based Reinforced End Decider.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that explicit room/object decoupling, knowledge from both a KG and CLIP, and a dedicated stopping module each contribute to the gains.
method: Room-Object Aware (ROA): explicitly decouples room- and object-related clues from the instruction and visual observations.

KERR+ (Knowledge-enabled Entity Relation Reasoning): uses structured knowledge from a knowledge graph and unstructured knowledge from a pretrained model to learn internal-external correlations among room and object entities.
Entity Prompter (EP): embedded in KERR+, it uses navigation history and visual entities as prompts to transfer knowledge from pretrained CLIP.
Reinforced End Decider (RED): learns the stopping scheme through a customised RL strategy and knowledge-enhanced matching.
Two additional techniques to improve navigation efficiency (details not given in the abstract).
